sources.entry: Heracles: Improving Resource Efficiency at Scale - Shows cache ways, cores, bandwidth and power must be partitioned together, or batch work reaches the tail.

summary.title: Heracles: Improving Resource Efficiency at Scale
summary.one_liner: Heracles is a feedback-based controller that coordinates hardware and software isolation (cache partitioning, per-core power, core scheduling, network traffic control) so best-effort batch tasks can safely colocate with latency-critical services like websearch.
takeaways: Low average server utilization (10% to 50%) in datacenters is largely due to latency-critical services with diurnal load, and colocating batch work can recover that capacity.
Interference on shared LLC, DRAM bandwidth, cores/HyperThreads, network and power is workload-dependent, so static partitioning is insufficient.
Heracles coordinates CAT cache partitioning, per-core frequency control, core scheduling and network traffic control in a local real-time feedback controller.
Reported results: about 90% effective machine utilization across colocation mixes and loads without SLO violations, and 15% to 300% throughput/TCO improvement on production Google servers.
The paper argues hardware support for DRAM bandwidth monitoring and isolation is needed, since none existed in commodity chips at the time.
summary.summary: The paper (ISCA 2015, Lo, Cheng, Govindaraju, Ranganathan and Kozyrakis) argues that latency-critical services leave servers underutilized, and that colocating best-effort batch tasks is blocked by interference on shared resources. It characterizes interference on production Google workloads (websearch, ml_cluster, memkeyval) using microbenchmarks that stress cores, LLC, DRAM bandwidth, network and power. It then presents Heracles, a real-time feedback controller that separates interference into subproblems and uses existing isolation mechanisms such as Intel CAT, per-core DVFS and traffic control. The evaluation on production servers reports about 90% utilization while meeting latency SLOs.
